task.title: Inspect exact schedule lifecycle history
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/821 by exposing one validated typed schedule history through deterministic read-only JSON.
acceptance_criteria: Add vela-dev schedule history for one validated exact schedule identity.
Emit typed entries in exact revision order and preserve null for a valid missing schedule.
Validate identity before storage access and escape exact untrusted lifecycle strings.
Fail closed without partial output, storage creation, mutation, clock, dispatch, or execution authority.

attempts.diagnostic: CLI integration tests failed because history was not a recognized schedule subcommand.
attempts.patch: Added full created-claim-release-claim-materialize ordering, cancellation, missing, escaping, invalid-ID, and missing-storage tests.

attempts.summary: Mapped validated typed history into deterministic JSON.
attempts.diagnostic: The kernel exposed complete typed history, but operators could not query one schedule without writing Rust.
attempts.patch: Validated ScheduleId before opening the read-only store, preserved the kernel's missing-stream distinction, and mapped each typed event locally without speculative abstraction.

attempts.summary: Completed exact-head review after a false-green pause.
attempts.diagnostic: The initial automatic CodeRabbit result was rate limited, so its success status did not constitute substantive review.
attempts.patch: Waited for the resumed four-file walkthrough, which found no actionable comments and confirmed validation, typed mapping, deterministic output, and bounded scope.

outcome.summary: Operators can inspect one schedule's complete typed lifecycle in exact revision order while preserving absence and failure distinctions.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo test --locked -p vela-dev --test cli

lessons: Expose already-validated typed history rather than raw event rows at the CLI boundary.
Preserve null for a missing aggregate so absence is not confused with an existing empty lifecycle.
Validate exact identities before filesystem access and preserve accepted strings without hidden normalization.
Keep a one-use event mapping local until real duplication justifies shared abstraction.
Require substantive review of the exact PR head before treating a successful review status as merge evidence.
